findings.text: follow-on: _equilibrium_resolved_defaults calls ResolvedForwardSolveDefaults.from_policy(request.policy) with no clip_mode, and this commit changed that parameter's default from the literal "chord" to a None sentinel that resolves forward_operator.support_clip_mode(); the transport receipt's equilibrium_resolved_defaults.clip_mode therefore now records the process global read at from_policy time rather than the request's own mode. Measured at head: under set_support_clip_mode("exact") from_policy(policy) returns clip_mode 'exact' while from_policy(policy, clip_mode="chord") returns 'chord', so an explicit clip_mode="chord" request handed to ForwardTransportInput.equilibrium_request records 'exact' in its transport resolved defaults -- the opposite of the mode it solved in -- where before this commit the literal default happened to record the request's chord correctly; pass clip_mode=request.clip_mode at the call site (as nova/equilibrium/forward.py:2686 already does) instead of letting the default resolve the process global, and this path is unguarded (tests/test_transport_forward_seam.py:51-88 asserts only the policy block of the resolved defaults).

follow-on: The gate exercises only the from_defaults construction route: it never constructs ForwardSolveRequest(...) directly, so the field(default_factory=_process_support_clip_mode) route at nova/equilibrium/solve_request.py:505 is untested, and it never calls ResolvedForwardSolveDefaults.from_policy with an omitted mode, so the None-sentinel route at :576 is untested; two of the three routes that the commit body, the landing and docs/evidence/fragments/forward-solve-api/fsapi-clip-mode-request-bridge.html advertise as repaired are therefore not evidenced. The negative-control arm was run against 'all three construction routes' but only the from_defaults mutation can move this assertion (the test builds both requests through from_defaults and reads the receipt through the explicit clip_mode=request.clip_mode pass-through at forward.py:2686), so the red arm cannot show the dataclass-factory or from_policy routes at all; add a direct-construction assertion and a from_policy-with-omitted-mode assertion, or narrow the advertised scope to the route the gate covers.

justifications.durability: The single commit 6de4568a1 carries a conventional subject and a body and no Co-Authored-By or tool trailer, and no plan, sprint or ticket label appears in the message, the changed source or the test; 19a76002e is an ancestor of 6de4568a1 so the work is a reachable child of the dispatch base; the lazy import of support_clip_mode avoids a module cycle and is the established pattern; the reviewed worktree is clean, so nothing is left uncommitted. A conventional subject and body with no trailer and a clean worktree is exactly the record the run recorded, so nothing is left to recover.
justifications.evidence: Every recorded number reproduces first-hand: the head bridge arm passes (1 passed in 5.78s, EXIT=0), the negative-control arm fails on the declared assertion (EXIT=1) at tests/test_forward_solve_clip_mode_bridge.py:86, the base arm base-test_route_solve_requests.log (rev 19a76002e, base-arm) and the head arm head-test_route_solve_requests.log both fail exactly test_request_execution_is_bit_identical_to_the_keyword_fixture, so zero failures are added; the from_policy behaviour I report was measured at head under set_support_clip_mode('exact') (omitted -> 'exact', explicit 'chord' -> 'chord'). It loses points because the 'three construction routes' claim is carried into the commit body, landing and fragment without a red arm that can see the dataclass-factory or from_policy routes, and there is no dispatch-base bridge log in test_logs, only the negative-control mutation as a stand-in for the base failing.
justifications.fit: The change follows house convention -- a mechanism-worded docstring, a default_factory rather than a mutable default, a lazy import to avoid the solve_request<->forward_operator cycle, and a test built on the existing _profile clip-mode fixture with the process global restored in a finally. It loses points because making from_policy's default read a process global turns a pure comparison helper into a context-dependent one and silently changed the transport caller, which the commit did not reconcile, so the receipt contract the plan is about now has a caller where the recorded mode and the executed mode can disagree.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The core repair is real and reproduces: an omitted clip_mode now resolves from forward_operator.support_clip_mode() on from_defaults, and the bridge gate passes 1/1 at head (1 passed in 5.78s) with the negative control failing (EXIT=1, assert omitted.clip_mode == 'exact' got 'chord'), while the pre-existing tests/test_forward_solve_clip_mode_request.py (1 passed) and tests/test_forward_support_clip_mode.py (3 passed) stay green. It loses points because the same semantic change is applied to ResolvedForwardSolveDefaults.from_policy, whose only non-from_dict caller outside equilibrium/forward.py -- nova/transport/forward.py:350 -- passes no clip_mode, so the transport receipt can now record the process global instead of the request's explicit mode, and only one of the three routes the record advertises is actually exercised.
justifications.scope_discipline: The commit touches exactly three paths and all three are inside the node's declared write paths (nova/equilibrium/solve_request.py, tests/test_forward_solve_clip_mode_bridge.py, docs/evidence/fragments/forward-solve-api/fsapi-clip-mode-request-bridge.html); no peer path, plan file or shared index is modified, the reviewed worktree is clean at the head, and the change is a focused 33-line edit plus a 90-line test and a 5-line anchor.
